belowGroundEvidence: The crane-track legs and the mooring block stand in the IJ harbour water about 2 m below the quay (Commons 29670110014, w03 panorama); the legs continue 1.0 m below the street datum so they never hang over the water surface.

throughPassages.evidence: The 1952 crane track is open underneath: between its legs the quay looks straight through to the marina and the water-side escape walkway (rectified panoramas recording_2024-10-23_07-33-22_00814 and TMX7316010203-002193_pano_0000_004912, artifacts/landmark-briefs/kraanspoor/w02-128*.jpg; Commons Kraanspoor.JPG). Only the four glazed stair cores and the lobbies beside them close it; the BAG ring is the glass box 11 m overhead.

The end blocks are four-legged open frames with two tie beams; the view along the track runs through them under the deck (Commons Amsterdam_-_Kraanspoor_(29670110014).jpg, head-on from the SW quay; w03-218 and w04-38 panoramas).

detachedStructures.evidence: Concrete mooring block with two bollards standing in the water off the SW head of the crane track (Commons Amsterdam_-_Kraanspoor_(30214778541).jpg and (29670110014).jpg).
